mcqs.question: What is the definition of wave motion?

options.A: Propagation of a disturbance through a medium with transfer of energy without net transport of matter
options.B: Movement of particles from one place to another
options.C: Oscillation of a single particle about its equilibrium position

mcqs.answer: Propagation of a disturbance through a medium with transfer of energy without net transport of matter
mcqs.explanation: Wave motion is the propagation of a disturbance that carries energy and information through oscillations of particles, but the particles themselves do not undergo a net displacement. Option A captures this definition, whereas the other options describe different phenomena.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes mechanical waves from electromagnetic waves?

options.A: Mechanical waves require a material medium, while electromagnetic waves can travel in vacuum
options.B: Mechanical waves travel at the speed of light, whereas electromagnetic waves are slower
options.C: Both types of waves need a material medium to propagate
options.D: Electromagnetic waves involve particle displacement, while mechanical waves involve electric fields

mcqs.answer: Mechanical waves require a material medium, while electromagnetic waves can travel in vacuum
mcqs.explanation: Mechanical waves (e.g., sound, water waves) need a material medium to transmit the disturbance. Electromagnetic waves (e.g., light, radio) consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields and can propagate through empty space. The other options are incorrect statements about speed, medium requirement, or the nature of the disturbances.

mcqs.question: In a transverse wave, the direction of particle displacement is:

options.A: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
options.B: Parallel to the direction of wave propagation

mcqs.answer: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
mcqs.explanation: In transverse waves, particles oscillate at right angles to the direction the wave travels (e.g., ripples on water, light waves). Option B describes longitudinal waves, while C and D are not characteristic of standard wave types.

mcqs.question: When a sound wave travels through air, the air particles primarily undergo which type of motion?

options.A: Longitudinal motion, compressing and rarefying along the direction of wave travel
options.B: Transverse motion, moving up and down perpendicular to the direction of travel
options.C: Circular motion around the propagation axis
options.D: No motion; only the wave travels

mcqs.answer: Longitudinal motion, compressing and rarefying along the direction of wave travel
mcqs.explanation: Sound waves are longitudinal; the particles of the medium oscillate back and forth in the same direction as the wave propagates, creating regions of compression and rarefaction. The other options describe motions not associated with sound in air.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches each term with its definition?

options.A: Wavelength – distance between successive crests; Frequency – number of cycles per second; Amplitude – maximum displacement from equilibrium; Period – time for one complete cycle
options.B: Wavelength – height of a crest; Frequency – time for one cycle; Amplitude – distance between crests; Period – number of cycles per second
options.C: Wavelength – time for one cycle; Frequency – distance between crests; Amplitude – number of cycles per second; Period – maximum displacement
options.D: Wavelength – speed of the wave; Frequency – energy of the wave; Amplitude – wavelength; Period – frequency

mcqs.answer: Wavelength – distance between successive crests; Frequency – number of cycles per second; Amplitude – maximum displacement from equilibrium; Period – time for one complete cycle
mcqs.explanation: Option A gives the standard definitions: wavelength is the spatial distance between two consecutive points in phase (e.g., crests), frequency is cycles per second (Hz), amplitude is the greatest displacement from the rest position, and period is the time for one cycle (inverse of frequency). The other options mix up the definitions.

mcqs.question: A stadium crowd performs the 'wave' where each person stands up and sits down sequentially. Which statement best describes this phenomenon?

options.A: It is an example of wave motion where energy is transferred across the stadium without net movement of people
options.B: People physically travel from one end of the stadium to the other
options.C: The crowd transfers mass from one side to the other
options.D: It is a static arrangement with no propagation

mcqs.answer: It is an example of wave motion where energy is transferred across the stadium without net movement of people
mcqs.explanation: The stadium 'wave' illustrates wave motion: the disturbance (standing up) moves around the stadium while each individual returns to the original position, so there is no net transport of matter. Options B, C, and D misrepresent the nature of the phenomenon.

mcqs.question: Some students think that because light can travel through vacuum, it must be a mechanical wave. Which statement correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: Light is an electromagnetic wave and does not require a material medium
options.B: Light is a mechanical wave that needs air to propagate
options.C: Mechanical waves always travel faster than light
options.D: Electromagnetic waves need a solid medium to travel

mcqs.answer: Light is an electromagnetic wave and does not require a material medium
mcqs.explanation: Light belongs to the electromagnetic spectrum; its oscillating electric and magnetic fields allow it to propagate in empty space. The other options are false: mechanical waves need a medium, they are generally slower than light, and electromagnetic waves do not need a solid medium.

mcqs.question: If a rope is shaken up and down at one end, a wave travels along the rope. Which observation confirms that this is a transverse wave?

options.A: The particles of the rope move up and down while the wave travels horizontally
options.B: The particles move forward in the same direction as the wave travels
options.C: The rope remains completely still as the wave passes
options.D: The speed of the wave does not depend on the tension in the rope

mcqs.answer: The particles of the rope move up and down while the wave travels horizontally
mcqs.explanation: In a transverse wave, particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, exactly as seen when the rope particles move vertically while the disturbance moves horizontally. Option B describes longitudinal motion, C is false, and D is unrelated to the transverse nature (wave speed does depend on tension).
